newsitem.title: USA: Clinton may veto budget over kid's care--Daschle.
newsitem.headline: Clinton may veto budget over kid's care--Daschle.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle said Monday President Clinton may veto balanced budget legislation if Republicans water down a provision extending health care to uninsured children.
"The president would veto that bill, if you minimize the child health provision," the South Dakota Democrat told reporters. "In my view the president has no choice."
House and Senate Republicans met Friday and will resume talks this week to work out a coordinated bargaining position on budget legislation cutting Medicare, Medicaid and other programs.

The measure, needed to implement a five-year budget deal between Congress and the White House, also includes billions of dollars for a new program to aid many of the nation's 10 million uninsured children.

The House provided $16 billion for the proposal, the Senate $24 billion, partly financed by a 20-cents-per-pack increase in the federal cigarette tax. Many House Republicans oppose the cigarette tax and its future is unclear.

Further, Republicans are moving away from the more stringent insurance standards in the Senate bill, which requires states to provide a set benefits package to children, including mental health coverage.

Instead, they are considering allowing states to choose from an list of insurance programs, some of which would provide less comprehensive coverage. States could also use the money to provide health services, rather than insurance.
Opponents charge the emerging plan might not provide an adequate standard of care and would provide incentives for states to abuse the system, using the new money to replace existing state services.
